loc: Green Canyon, San Bernardino National Forest (near  Big Bear), San Bernardino County, California
rmk:
The bird was calling while perched on a snag about 40 meters from the edge of the road where I stood while recording it.  I could see its eye shine with a headlamp and I could also see the bird's silhouette against the bright moonlit sky with binoculars.  The bird flew out several times and returned to the same perch.  It also perched silently for up to several minutes at a time.  

Conditions were quite windy, probably 3-4 on the Beaufort scale, with branches and even whole trees swaying.  Among the recordings I obtained, this one had the strongest signal-to-noise ratios and (for the most part) the least interference due to wind.  

Habitat: mixed conifers such as white firs and pines (Jeffrey and/or Ponderosa), some willows along a creek, and open areas among the trees.

The Moon was 3/4 full tonight.  Skies were clear.  Temperature was about 13 deg C.  There were a lot of bugs in the air.

Recorded with an Olympus LS-10S equipped with a Sennheiser MKE-400 short shotgun microphone.

loc: Aptos, Santa Cruz, California
rmk: Seen and heard at Valencia Creek Ranch (private property, restricted access) by a party of 25 people. Soon after the bird started calling, some of us, led by Logan Kahle, walked out the mowed path that contours above the clearing to get a better listen. At one point, the path passes through a grassy opening before plunging into woodland. About 8:45, Logan had traversed the opening and was peering ahead into the woodland while I remained on the other side of the opening. I whispered loudly "turn around!" because the Whip-Poorwill had flown up, started circling the opening, and was hovering mothlike behind Logan's head. The bird was a goatsucker by shape, flight style, and coloration. It was a bit larger than a Common Poorwill, with a longer, spatula-shaped tail that showed large rectangular white corners. It called incessantly, moving up and down the slope
